subjects.label: Studio closed days after launch
subjects.description: The developer shutting down within days of release, going bankrupt and leaving the game with nobody to fix it; not the accusation that this was deliberate fraud, which has its own row.

subjects.label: Scam and fraud accusations
subjects.description: Calling the release a scam, a rug pull or a con and the developers liars or fraudsters who took the money and ran; not the closure as an event, and not plain complaints about the price.

subjects.label: The studio behind the game
subjects.description: Talk about the developer itself: where it comes from and jibes at its origin, its staff and hiring, its five years of work and its public statements; not the shutdown or the fraud charge as such.

subjects.label: Trailers versus the delivered game
subjects.description: The gap between what the trailers, videos and store pitch promised and what shipped: sold as an open-world MMO survival game and nothing like the footage; not the genre it turned out to be, which has its own row.

subjects.label: Extraction shooter in the Tarkov mould
subjects.description: What kind of game it actually is: an extraction shooter measured against Tarkov and other survival games, with token survival systems; not whether the marketing was honest about it.

subjects.label: Server capacity and logging in
subjects.description: Getting into the game at all in the first days: full servers in every region, failed logins, being unable to join friends and having to share a server to group up; not lag or matchmaking once inside.

subjects.label: Unfinished state and potential
subjects.description: The game shipping as a raw alpha that should not have entered early access yet, and the hope or doubt that it has the potential to be finished one day; not how much content there is as such.

subjects.label: Hype, waiting and expectations
subjects.description: The years of anticipation and delays before release, and whether the letdown was foreseeable given them; not the state of the game itself.

subjects.label: Refunds after the collapse
subjects.description: Asking how to get the money back, demanding it, or arguing against refunding so the developers can carry on; not whether the price was fair in the first place.
